headline: On this date in 1947, Jackie Robinson made his MLB debut with the Brooklyn Dodgers, breaking baseball's color barrier.
On this date in 1935, the Reds beat the Phillies 2-1 at Crosley Field in MLB's first night game — President Roosevelt flipped the switch from the White House.
On this date in 1933, MLB held its first All-Star Game at Comiskey Park; the AL beat the NL 4-2 and Babe Ruth hit the first All-Star home run.
On this date in 1974, Hank Aaron hit his 715th career home run off Al Downing, passing Babe Ruth for the all-time record.
On this date in 1961, Roger Maris hit his 61st home run off Tracy Stallard, breaking Babe Ruth's single-season record.
On this date in 1998, Mark McGwire hit his 62nd home run off Steve Trachsel, breaking Roger Maris's 37-year-old single-season record.
On this date in 1939, Lou Gehrig pulled himself from the Yankees lineup, ending his consecutive games streak at 2,130.
On this date in 1995, Cal Ripken Jr. played in his 2,131st consecutive game, breaking Lou Gehrig's 56-year-old record.
On this date in 1970, Tom Seaver struck out 19 Padres including the last 10 batters in a row — a consecutive-strikeout record that still stands.
On this date in 1998, rookie Kerry Wood struck out 20 Astros in his 5th career start — a one-hit, no-walk shutout that tied Roger Clemens's nine-inning record.
On this date in 1956, Don Larsen threw the only perfect game in World Series history, retiring all 27 Dodgers in Game 5.
On this date in 1993, Lee Smith recorded his 358th career save, passing Jeff Reardon to become MLB's all-time saves leader.
On this date in 2006, Trevor Hoffman recorded his 479th career save against the Pirates, passing Lee Smith to become MLB's all-time saves leader.
On this date in 2011, Mariano Rivera recorded his 602nd career save against the Twins, passing Trevor Hoffman to become MLB's all-time saves leader.
On this date in 2007, Barry Bonds hit his 756th career home run off Mike Bacsik, passing Hank Aaron to become MLB's all-time home run leader.
On this date in 1985, Pete Rose singled off Eric Show for his 4,192nd career hit, passing Ty Cobb to become MLB's all-time hits leader.
On this date in 1991, Rickey Henderson stole his 939th career base, passing Lou Brock to become MLB's all-time stolen base leader.
On this date in 2022, Aaron Judge hit his 62nd home run of the season, breaking Roger Maris's 61-year-old American League single-season home run record.
